record.original_question: Extend the theory of virtual covers so that it applies effectively to classical knots in S^3, relate virtual-cover invariants to Milnor mu-invariants and possibly to one-component links, understand how virtual covers behave under local moves such as crossing changes, self-Delta moves, and Z-moves, determine whether virtual covers can detect mutations, and characterize exactly which moves on two-component links preserve the associated virtual-knot type.

evidence.quote: Is there an extension of the theory of virtual covers to one component links (i.e. knots) in S^3.
Use virtual covers to find a relation between the Milnor mu-invariants and invariants of virtual knots.
How well does a virtual knot associated to a virtual cover of a classical link behave under local moves (non-isotopy) applied to the link?
Find a complete set of moves on such two component links which do not change the virtual isotopy type of the associated virtual knot.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A two-component link L = J ∪ K in S^3 with J an unknot determines, via the standard "virtual cover" construction, a virtual knot v(L): one removes a tubular neighborhood of J, identifies its complement with a thickened surface Σ × I (where Σ is a genus-one surface arising from the unknotted component), and represents K inside Σ × I; the resulting virtual knot type v(L) ∈ V is the virtual cover of L associated to J. More generally, given a classical link in S^3 and an unknotted sublink U whose complement is homeomorphic to Σ × I for some surface Σ, the virtual cover construction associates a virtual knot (or virtual link) to the remaining components.

Address the following collection of questions about the theory of virtual covers.

(1) Extend the construction so that it produces effective invariants for one-component classical links, i.e. classical knots in S^3, rather than requiring a multi-component setting.

(2) For an n-component classical link L (n ≥ 2) with vanishing Milnor μ̄-invariants of length ≤ k, establish a precise relationship between the higher Milnor μ̄-invariants of L and invariants of the virtual knot v(L) obtained as a virtual cover. In particular, exhibit virtual-knot invariants whose values recover or are determined by specified Milnor μ̄-invariants of L.

(3) Determine the behavior of v(L) under local moves on the classical link L, including: (a) crossing changes between two components; (b) self-Δ moves (Δ-moves involving three strands of the same component); and (c) Z-moves. For each move, identify which classical moves on L correspond to which moves on v(L) in the virtual category, and which leave the virtual isotopy type of v(L) unchanged.

(4) Decide whether the virtual cover v(L) detects mutation, i.e. whether there exist mutant classical links L and L' with v(L) ≠ v(L') as virtual knots, or prove that v is invariant under all classical mutations.

(5) For two-component classical links L = J ∪ K with J an unknot, find a complete set of local moves on L (a finite list of moves such that any two such links L, L' with v(L) = v(L') as virtual knots are connected by a finite sequence of these moves) that exactly characterizes the equivalence relation L ∼ L' ⇔ v(L) = v(L').
artifact.status_search_result: Related work has appeared on Milnor-type concordance invariants for virtual knots in thickened surfaces and on welded Milnor invariants of string links, which provides partial progress related to (2). However, no source clearly resolves the full program of questions (extension to one-component links, behavior under crossing changes/self-Δ/Z-moves, mutation detection, and a complete set of moves preserving v(L) for two-component links). The status of the overall problem appears to remain open or only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Milnor's concordance invariants for knots on surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Extended μ̄-invariants are defined for knots in thickened surfaces and obstruct concordance to homologically trivial knots.
status_evidence.claim: Milnor μ̄-invariants have been extended to virtual/thickened-surface knots, providing partial progress on connecting Milnor invariants and virtual-knot invariants.

status_evidence.title: Arrow calculus for welded and classical links
status_evidence.snippet: Welded Milnor invariants of string links are finite-type, and restrictions to classical objects yield Goussarov–Vassiliev invariants.
status_evidence.claim: There is partial work tying Milnor invariants of classical links to invariants of welded/virtual objects, relevant but not equivalent to virtual covers.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Seifert Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops virtual cover/Seifert surface theory for links.
status_evidence.claim: The virtual cover framework continues to be developed, but the listed problems are not announced as solved.
